claims.claim: Laya (NandhaKishorM) is created 2026-09-18, not 2023; HF repo created 2026-09-18
claims.locator: GitHub API created_at; HF API createdAt (B-03)
claims.values: GitHub created 2026-09-18T04:46:33Z; HF convaiinnovations/laya created 2026-09-18T05:05:55Z; receptron/laya 2026-09-19T15:30:52Z
claims.limits: dates are repo/HF creation, not training date; README author blog hints at an earlier internal 'a year ago' build (headline seen only as a badge title, not read)

claims.claim: Two real Laya GitHub repos exist with different roles: NandhaKishorM/laya is the model author's main repo (Python, PyPI laya, HF convaiinnovations); receptron/laya is a third-party Node/TS ONNX runtime
claims.values: receptron README: upstream model convaiinnovations/laya; ONNX bundle receptron/laya-onnx; request shape matches Python RLAgent.system_one and TypeSafe Jev system_one
claims.limits: README also says weights by Convai Innovations; GitHub owner NandhaKishorM is a user account; the NandhaKishorM README does not state the link to the convaiinnovations org beyond HF links and the model card linking back to that repo
claims.checks_gpt: CONFLICT: R1/CHAT NandhaKishorM/laya vs R2 receptron/laya

claims.claim: Laya license: GitHub repo Apache-2.0; HF weights Apache-2.0; receptron runtime code MIT with weights Apache-2.0
claims.locator: HF API license tag; B-01 LICENSE; B-02 README
claims.values: NandhaKishorM/laya: Apache-2.0 (code); convaiinnovations/laya: apache-2.0 (weights); receptron/laya: MIT (code); receptron/laya-onnx: apache-2.0
claims.checks_gpt: R2 'code MIT / weights Apache-2.0' is true only of the receptron runtime; the model's own repo is Apache-2.0 for code too

claims.claim: Laya sizes and base: three checkpoints, English laya 421M (ModernBERT-large, ctx 512), laya-multilingual 322M (mmBERT-base, ctx 1024, up to 8192), laya-typed-decisions 421M (fine-tune of ModernBERT-large, ctx 1024); about 2.3 GB total
claims.values: 421M / 322M / 421M params; HF English file ~808 MB, multilingual ~647 MB
claims.limits: table relayed by summariser

claims.claim: Laya ONNX bundle by receptron is ~1.7 GB fp32, loaded on Node 20+, about 2 GB RAM advised
claims.limits: README does not say which of the three checkpoints the ONNX bundle holds (the 1.7 GB is a single bundle, not 2.3 GB total)

claims.claim: Laya architecture: non-autoregressive encoder with decision head, trained with RL against strictly proper scoring rules (RLCD); a Router picks a checkpoint per request
claims.values: ModernBERT-large / mmBERT-base backbone; decision head from scratch

claims.claim: Laya latency on T4: 39.5 ms (English) and 32.8 ms (multilingual) for one question; 10 questions 158.6 / 72.3 ms; 50 questions 771 / 337 ms; headline 33 ms single, 7.2 ms/question batched
claims.locator: model card latency table; B-01 README
claims.limits: 'P50 33 ms' in GPT wording is the multilingual checkpoint (32.8) and the headline; English is 39.5 ms. Cloudflare's own table lists Laya median 5.8 ms / p95 222.5 ms with no hardware (B-12)

claims.claim: Laya typed-decisions benchmark (2,000 decisions): fine-tuned laya-typed-decisions 0.766 accuracy vs TypeSafe Jev 1.13.0 at 0.727; Jev figure is third-party published, never measured by Laya authors
claims.locator: model card Benchmarks; B-01 README comparison
claims.values: 0.766 vs 0.727 accuracy; base laya 0.362, base laya-multilingual 0.342; soft accuracy favours Jev 0.580 vs 0.471
claims.limits: 0.766 is after fine-tuning on that benchmark's own split; zero-shot Laya is at 0.362, below a 0.461 majority baseline (per OrcaRouter); the 0.727 for Jev is not a same-harness run
claims.checks_gpt: R2 'fine-tuned 0.766 accuracy on typed-decisions vs Jev 0.727'

claims.claim: Laya vs Jev other comparisons: AG News 0.950 vs 0.910; DAIR Emotion 0.595 vs 0.480; Banking77 (77 labels) 0.425 vs 0.870 (Jev wins above 20 options); ECE post-temperature 0.081 vs 0.246 in one table, but the typed-decisions table shows ECE 0.213 vs Jev 0.144
claims.locator: model card Benchmarks; B-01 README comparison and typed-decisions tables (README says tables not reconciled)
claims.limits: internal inconsistency in ECE between two README tables; Jev values are third-party

claims.claim: OrcaRouter article: Laya calibration error falls 0.466 -> 0.081 after per-question-type temperature refit; Jev reported 0.246; the '4.69B' model compared is RSI-Jev v6.1-VL (Qwen3.5-4B-Base), not TypeSafe Jev
claims.values: ECE-like 'calibration error' 0.466 -> 0.081; Laya 421M vs RSI-Jev 4.69B; Laya zero-shot 0.362 typed-decisions; RSI-Jev 50.98 on Decision Index 0.3; RSI-Jev 22.5 ms (low effort) / ~40 ms (full) on H200; Laya p50 32.8 ms T4
claims.limits: article states neither project was benchmarked against the other; publisher sells Jev; 10 of RSI-Jev's 15 benchmarks contributed training data. Date 2026-10-08, URL zh-CN served English text
claims.checks_gpt: OrcaRouter 'Laya 421M fine-tuned vs Jev 4.69B zero-shot' (CHAT/R2): the 4.69B is RSI-Jev, an open third-party model, not TypeSafe's Jev

claims.claim: Laya exposes a Jev-compatible API: POST /v1/systemone (laya.serve); existing Jev client only needs a base URL change; documented differences: token budget not 255-option cap, 100 options cap, score levels need descriptions, confidence = 1 - normalised entropy

Laya languages: multilingual checkpoint targets 100+ languages; on T4 benchmark 48 of 51 languages usable (>3x random) for multilingual vs 23 of 51 for English; English checkpoint scores 0.000 on Khmer at 0.952 raw confidence
claims.values: MASSIVE intent English 0.783 / multilingual 0.657; XNLI English 0.860 / multilingual 0.843; 17,416 questions
claims.limits: '100+ languages' is a model-card claim; measured on 51 languages

claims.claim: Laya release/status: PyPI package, v0.4.13 released 2026-10-21; releases v0.4.9 (10-17) through v0.4.13 (10-21); 34k stars
claims.limits: README claims 2,461 commits in ~5 weeks; star count looks unusually high; not investigated

claims.claim: Laya input modalities: text only (English/multilingual); no image input

claims.claim: Kev-27B vs Jev: Decision Index (breadth-v1) Kev-27B v2 52.3, v1 50.2, Jev 54.0; accuracy on new sources dev 0.851 / test 0.889 vs Jev 0.857 dev; README says 'within a point' but not a controlled comparison
